wu: Subject Charades: Teacher writes 5 school subjects on the board (Math, Art, Science, PE, English). Students take turns miming the subject while others guess, saying 'You like [subject]!' or 'It's [subject]!'
wuAlt: Subject Bingo: Teacher calls out subjects, students cross them on a 3x3 grid with pictures. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Subject Speed Chat: Students walk around and ask 'What subject is this?' pointing to a flashcard, then reply 'I like it!' or 'I don't like it!'
pres: Teacher shows flashcards of school subjects, models 'I like Math because it's fun' and 'I don't like Science because it's difficult'. Students repeat chorally. Teacher asks 'Do you like Math?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Subject Survey: Teacher walks around asking 'Do you like Art?', students respond with thumbs up/down. Teacher tallies on the board, modeling 'Three students like Art.'
Mini-Story: Teacher tells a short story about a student who likes PE but doesn't like History, using gestures for 'like' and 'don't like'.
prac: Subject Popularity Graph: Teams of 3 receive a graph with subjects on the x-axis. They ask classmates 'Do you like [subject]?', tally responses, and draw bars. Teams report 'Most students like Art!'
pracAlt: Subject Debate Mini: Teams debate 'Math is better than Art'. Each student says 'I like [subject] because...' with one reason. Teacher times 1-minute turns.
Find Someone Who...: Students walk around with a grid, asking 'Do you like Science?', writing names of those who say 'Yes'.
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a student's favorite subject: 'He likes Art because he can draw pictures.' Students draw the subject and reason, then compare in pairs.
re: Subject Jump: Teacher calls out a subject (e.g., 'PE!'), students jump if they like it, crouch if they don't. Teacher asks 'Why?' after each round.
prod: Interview a Classmate: Students pair up, ask 'What's your favorite subject? Why?', then report back to the class: 'Fatima likes History because it's interesting.'
rw: Read a short text about a student's week, answer 3 questions: 'What subject does he like? Why? What subject doesn't he like?' Students write answers in full sentences.
st: Spooky Story Chain: Pairs write one paragraph about a haunted school, using 'I like/don't like [subject]' (e.g., 'I don't like History because the ghosts talk!'). Read aloud with lights off. End with 'Today we learned to say what subjects we like and why. Thank you, class!'
g: Students describe a subject without saying its name or 3 taboo words (e.g., for Math: 'numbers, plus, calculator').
Match subject flashcards with 'like/don't like' cards, saying sentences like 'I like Art!'.
Two teams race to write 5 subjects they like on the board, saying 'I like [subject]!' for each.
Teacher says a subject, students spell it. If correct, they say 'I like [subject]!'.
Teacher posts subjects in corners, students go to their favorite and say 'I like [subject] because...'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more reasons why they like/dislike a subject.
Support: Use sentence frames 'I like [subject] because it's...' with word bank (fun, easy, interesting).
hw: Write 6 sentences about your favorite subject (e.g., 'I like English. It's fun. I don't like Math. It's difficult.')
Draw your ideal classroom with your favorite subjects, label 3 items.
Interview a family member about their school subjects, write 2 sentences.
tip: Use Moroccan school examples (e.g., 'I like Arabic because it's my language') to build cultural relevance. Keep sentences short and repeat 'because' often for reinforcement.
